category_title: Grade 1 students who struggle with writing and self-regulation but benefit from oral discourse
minimal_context: Joshua is working independently at his desk to write down his findings from a mass measurement activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Now that you and your partner finished the mass measurement activity, please work independently to write down your findings on your paper.

STUDENT: (Stares at the blank paper and puts his pencil down) I don't know what to put down.

TUTOR: Just think about what you measured and write it down.

STUDENT: (Leans over his desk to look at the student sitting next to him) What did you write for the blocks?

TUTOR: Joshua, please focus on your own paper and do your own work.

STUDENT: (Quickly scribbles down letters from his neighbor's paper, copying the words incorrectly) I'm just putting what he has.

options.A: Incorporate frequent opportunities for him to respond (OTRs) during the mass measurement instruction and subsequent independent writing tasks.
options.B: Provide individual storage space, such as chair bags or desks with compartments, to organize his measurement materials during independent work.
options.C: Provide supplemental instruction in academic engagement skills, such as organizational skills, requesting assistance, and taking brief breaks during independent writing.
options.D: Allow him to present to the class and engage in discourse about the measurement process until he can explain his findings to his satisfaction.
